title: One payment request can still leave two approval cards, and the agent then reports an outcome that matches neither
root_cause: Suspected. Three walkers (R1, J2, V2) saw two identical $1,250 cards for one request, one Approved and one Denied, and an agent message 'not submitted: denied' next to an Approved card. All walked the same shared Mercury thread at the same time and may each have asked for the payment, so two legitimate requests are possible. Commit d865d7484 ('Keep one live approval card per payment request when a run resumes') merged at 02:34, shortly before the walks, and it is not known whether the running API had it loaded. P0 is not supported: no walker saw money move or a card resolve without a click this iteration (the iteration-10 'relayed Yes resolves a card' concern was not seen again). Stays P1 until a single-user repro.
verification: Suspected. Code: the pause path is packages/adapters/src/executor.ts:3980-4010 (pauseForAsk). 'No longer active' wording exists in apps/web/src/components/AskCard.tsx and apps/mobile/app/thread.tsx, so the superseded-card state exists. Not reproduced by one user. First step is to restart the API and worker from current main, then repeat with one user.
files: packages/adapters/src/executor.ts (pauseForAsk, resume; only if the repro still shows two live cards)
packages/adapters/src/executor-approval-replay.test.ts (regression: resume reuses the pending card; denying a superseded card does not rewrite an approved outcome)
apps/web/e2e/approval-resume.spec.ts (already covers resume; extend if needed)
reach: Anyone who lets an agent pay a bill. A wrong or contradictory result is about money.
acceptance_criteria: Repro with one user on a clean thread after restarting API and worker from main: ask for one payment, reload mid-run, press Send once: exactly one live card, any older card reads 'No longer active' and cannot be pressed.
Final agent message names the outcome of the approved card only.
If the repro stays clean, close the cluster as 'two walkers, two requests' and say so in the PR.
reopens: iteration 10 C1 (was P0, falls to P1 as that cluster specified)

title: Legal Done and Dismiss show no Undo line: the line is rendered inside the list that the refetch just removed the row from
root_cause: Confirmed in code. LegalDeadlines.tsx close() calls onChanged() (overview.reload) after setting undo. The server returns only open deadlines (apps/api/src/legal.ts:51, status open), so after the reload `deadlines` no longer contains the closed row and the undo slot, which is rendered inside deadlines.map (line 151-162), never appears. J2 saw no Undo at 0 s, 1 s and in 3 screenshots. A mis-tap on Done cannot be reversed.
verification: Observed by J2 (3 rows) and confirmed in code: apps/web/src/pages/legal/LegalDeadlines.tsx:62-70 (reload after close), :151-162 (undo rendered only for rows still in `deadlines`), apps/api/src/legal.ts:51 (open only). Iteration 9 J2-04 and iteration 10 J2-07 were dropped as 'Undo exists, 30 s'; that claim was true only before the refetch was added.
files: apps/web/src/pages/legal/LegalDeadlines.tsx (render the undo line from the `undo` state at the closed row's position, not from the refetched list; or keep closed rows in local state until the timer ends)
apps/web/src/pages/legal/LegalDeadlines.stories.tsx (story with a parent that drops the row on onChanged)
a unit test with a parent that removes the row after onChanged
reach: Every Legal user who closes a deadline.
acceptance_criteria: Failing test first: parent removes the deadline on onChanged; the 'Marked ... done. Undo' line is still shown.
Undo restores the row in its place within 30 s; after 30 s the line disappears.
Row height does not jump when the line replaces the row.
reopens: iteration 9 J2-04 and iteration 10 J2-07 (wrongly dropped)

title: Chief's first answer states counts while the mailbox is still being sorted, and says one thing in two bubbles
root_cause: Chief delegates to the Inbox agent and relays its answer even when the sort has not finished, so a new user is told, in bold, that no emails need a reply and there are no open to-dos. Two minutes later Inbox shows 9 and 5. Not located in code; suspected in the delegation prompt or relay.

files: apps/api/src/inbox-agent.ts or the Inbox tools in packages/adapters (find where counts are read; grep triage status)
Chief delegation prompt / relay (apps/api/src/chief*.ts or executor relay)
packages/adapters/src/executor.ts only if the two-bubble duplicate comes from the relay
reach: Every new user whose first question is asked during the first sort (the recommended first-run path).
acceptance_criteria: While the first sort is running, the answer says Praci is still sorting the mail and gives no counts.

title: Money requests through Chief give instructions that are wrong or contradict each other
root_cause: The agent text for a failed or pending payment is partly fixed wording, not the tool's real reason. J2: Chief says 'Turn on Allow changes for Mercury under Integrations' while that switch is already on and the real problem is a missing recipient; the Mercury agent then ends with 'Open Settings', which cannot add a recipient. V2: Chief posts an interim 'asked Mercury to pay $300 ... no confirmation yet' and then 'Mercury did not submit ... a different payment ($1,250) is pending', so Maya cannot tell whether anything is pending.
verification: Observed by J2, V2, R1. Fixed wording is at apps/api/src/finance-agent.ts:14-15 and apps/api/src/integration-agent.ts:27; the 'Open Settings' link near packages/adapters/src/executor.ts ~8358 (R1 reading, not re-verified).
files: apps/api/src/finance-agent.ts:14-15 and apps/api/src/integration-agent.ts:27 (report the tool's actual reason; drop the fixed 'turn on Allow changes' sentence unless the switch is off)
packages/adapters/src/executor.ts near the no-recipient reply (link to Contacts, not Settings)
Chief relay prompt (one outcome message per request; replace the interim message when the final one arrives)
reach: Anyone paying a bill through Chief.
acceptance_criteria: A missing recipient is reported as a missing recipient with a link to Contacts (or no link); 'Allow changes' is named only when it is off.
Chief posts one outcome per payment request: requested, not submitted (with reason) or approved.
Chief tells the user to ask the Mercury agent when Chief itself lacks access.
